title: Malacca Sultanate
summary: A lineage claiming the heritage of Srivijaya founded the port of Melaka on the strait between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea around 1400. Its first three rulers travelled to the Ming court at Nanjing, and Admiral Zheng He made Melaka one of his main Southeast Asian bases. The court adopted Islam in the 1420s, drawing Arab, Persian and Indian Muslim traders, and by Sultan Mansur's reign (1459-1477) Melaka was the dominant entrepot of the straits. Albuquerque's Portuguese fleet conquered it in 1511.

uncertainty.note: Founded around 1400 (accounts range from c. 1399 to 1402) by Parameswara; conquered by Afonso de Albuquerque's Portuguese fleet in August 1511.

as_recorded.value: established the port of Melaka around 1400

where.historical_name: Malacca, capital of the Malacca Sultanate (Kesultanan Melayu Melaka)

importance.justification: The leading port of the Malacca Strait, which spread Islam and Malay court culture through maritime Southeast Asia (R3 D3 T3 L2).

related.because: Portuguese naval forces captured the capital in 1511, dissolving the sultanate and driving the court into exile.
